drafts.headline: #GhostedByMyClient: small business owners share no-show stories
drafts.angle: Owners are venting about no-shows; the useful answer is what goes with fewer of them, measured across real bookings.
drafts.comment: In September, 7.9% of 412,000 salon appointments on our platform were no-shows, but bookings where the salon took a deposit had a 3.1% no-show rate. The part owners can control is asking clients to commit at the moment they book, and saying plainly what happens if they don't come.

drafts.headline: State consumer agency proposes rule requiring salons and clinics to disclose no-show fees before booking
drafts.angle: What the rule means in practice: owners can keep deposits, which go with far fewer no-shows, as long as clients see them before they book.
drafts.comment: Across 412,000 salon appointments on our platform in September, bookings that took a deposit had a 3.1% no-show rate, against 7.9% across all of them. Whatever happens to the rule, owners lose nothing by showing the fee before the client books, and the clients who commit up front are the ones who turn up.

drafts.headline: Carrier outage delayed text messages for six hours, including appointment reminders
drafts.angle: What a small business should do the morning after reminders failed to arrive.
drafts.comment: Last night was a reminder that a text is only one channel. Of 1,840,000 reminder texts our customers sent in September, 61.0% got a confirming reply, so a lost batch matters. Owners should check this morning's confirmations and call anyone who hasn't answered.
